title: GTA 6 Nearly Hit With Ban Over ‘Frequent Male Genital Exposure’

News Hog wild GTA 6 nearly hit with ban over ‘frequent male genital exposure’ Graphic: Grant Walkup/Polygon | Source images: Rockstar Games Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Grand Theft Auto 6 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap With the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 mere days away, we already know to expect a whole lot of mature subject matter. Official promotional materials like the Netflix Extended Look have prominently featured strip clubs, drug deals gone wrong, and chaotic vehicular shootouts. A new report out of South Korea from Inven Global claims members of the Game Content Rating Board (GCRB) nearly refused to issue a rating for GTA 6 , which would have effectively banned the game there. The main sticking point? An excessive amount of "out of context genital nudity." Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover According to the report, the GCRB held three separate review sessions to determine its rating for GTA 6 . The first review took place on Sept. 10, before committee members had access to a playable build. That ended in a tie, with three voting in favor of refusal and three in favor of an Adults Only rating. "I do not believe genital exposure to this extent falls within acceptable limits under the current standard," said one of the members who refused a rating. It's possible that this assessment was shaped by the massive GTA 6 gameplay leaks that took place over the summer, which showed Jason interacting with unclothed patrons at a nudist resort and nonchalantly cruising around the streets of Miami with his dong hanging out . The GCRB met again on Oct. 2, but ultimately opted to postpone its decision a second time, having obtained a copy of the game just a few days earlier. "Further inspection is necessary, but if a rating is actually granted, we should take this opportunity to review changing the regulation that treats simple genital exposure as grounds for refusal," said one of the committee members. Image: Rockstar Games During the final review session on Oct. 16, the committee voted eight to one in favor of issuing an Adults Only (19+) rating. "It appears that they intentionally covered genital exposure in explicitly sexual scenes, while allowing exposure in background settings," explained one voter from the majority. The lone dissenter expressed concerns that this would mean open season on background penises in future games. "Suppose we consider genre characteristics to permit background genital exposure in adventures or RPGs while remaining conservative only with suggestive games," they said. "I am concerned that background genital exposure will frequently appear in future RPGs as a result." Don't get any ideas, Square Enix! What can we learn from the great dong debate? While it is pretty funny to imagine people having high-stakes debates about how much dong is too much dong for a video game, this conflict indirectly tells us some interesting things about GTA 6. We know there will "explicitly sexual scenes" in the game, but you won't see anyone's business district during those moments. In other words, Rockstar isn't bringing the infamous Hot Coffee sex minigame from GTA: San Andreas into 2026. That's probably for the best. GTA 6 has received strict adult age classifications in virtually every market. It's got an M (17+) rating in North America, and 18+ ratings in Japan, Europe, the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, South Africa, Taiwan, Thailand, and Brazil. The game has a 21+ rating in Saudi Arabia and the UAE. GTA 6 will be released on Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.
